body:
@JohnnyWilson16 I followed up on the custom-init/defaulted-alias regression from #9343 with a load-only repair prototype and additional compatibility checks (AI-assisted execution).

[Pinned patch, runnable tests and raw outputs](https://github.com/flyoung588/recursive-productive-capacity/tree/b64d0d90e1e6ff42956b5aa847571cb763cbd7a6/co-do-003/round2)

The prototype builds on your `model_validate(..., by_name=True)` approach. For custom initializers it re-keys **simple string validation aliases** before validation, unless the model already accepts names or disables alias validation. It keeps the stored payload unchanged, does not mutate model configuration, and still executes the custom initializer. The five direct cases from my earlier comment now pass. An additional seven controls pass, including extra fields, name-only validation, and AIMessage/ToolMessage/HumanMessage. The official checkpoint suite excluding unavailable Redis integration gives **252 passed** on current main `eb8ec111b3e9d3108af5d7bdcac51e3e913637a0`, Python 3.11.12 / Pydantic 2.12.5.

**It is not a complete repair:** a custom-initialized aliased model nested inside a normal model still restores 42 as 1. The new boundary suite deliberately retains that failure: **7 passed, 1 failed**. General recursive aliases, unions, and arbitrary constructor transformations are not covered, so I would not propose merging this prototype as a general solution. The logs also retain an initial name-only-validation regression that the configuration guard fixed.

Would you be interested in incorporating/adapting these tests into your existing PR, and deciding the reconstruction contract for nested custom initializers together? I can continue testing a revised candidate against these cases. I have not opened a competing PR; #9352 is still closed and unmerged pending maintainer assignment. Maintainer assignment of the existing author would preserve the current contribution path, if that is the desired scope.

---
Round-3 boundary update (2026-10-28): [eight executable constructor/alias counterexamples and raw observations](https://github.com/flyoung588/recursive-productive-capacity/tree/4c4fe173dc58c0dc47bcf54858dbe4244e7f65a7/co-do-003/round3), run against unchanged upstream, your serializer hunk, and the scoped prototype above.

Nested custom-init aliases, a discriminated-Union branch, and custom-init AliasChoices/AliasPath remain lossy. More fundamentally, a constructor that doubles its input stores 42 from original input 21, then restores 84 when the stored field is passed through that constructor again. A constructor that rejects stored 42 instead yields an equal-valued object through the serializer's existing model_construct fallback, with **zero successful custom-initializer executions**. Equality-only round-trip checks therefore hide the very constructor bypass we want to avoid. The probe observes this existing fallback; it does not add or recommend it.

I am stopping extension of the scoped prototype rather than presenting recursive key rewriting as a general fix. Arbitrary post-init state cannot be transparently treated as constructor input without an explicit reconstruction contract. This does not rule out your ordinary alias fix or a narrower agreed contract. The artifact includes one-command reproduction with separate processes and unchanged-source restoration; no complete fix, new upstream PR, or constructor-preserving success is claimed. The unchanged-source checkpoint baseline remains 252 passed excluding unavailable Redis service tests; that is not validation of a new repair.
